sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface labeling confirmed by DogTag-specific reagent on intact cells; full functional characterization of this exact construct not separately reported in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names Y460–N461 as the junction in full-length, membrane-anchored TRPC5. Python confirms seq[459]='Y' and seq[460]='N', both within the extracellular span 455–476 (ECL3). The junction is 6 residues from the TM4 C-boundary (454) and 16 residues from the TM5 N-boundary (477), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance on both sides. The DogTag itself (~22 aa with linkers) is within the 13–23 aa target range. Full-length human TRPC5 with DogTag (DIPATYEFTDGKHYITNEPIPPK) flanked by GGGGS linkers inserted between Y460 and N461 by site-directed mutagenesis; construct also carries C-terminal SYFP2. Used in HEK cells to assess surface labeling of the intact, membrane-anchored channel.

sources.claim: For pcDNA4-TRPC5-DogTag-SYFP2, DogTag (underlined), flanked by a glycine-serine linkers (GGGGS DIPATYEFTDGKHYITNEPIPPK GGGGS) was introduced between Y460 and N461 of human TRPC5 by site-directed mutagenesis with Q5 High-Fidelity DNA polymerase (NEB).

sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)
ordered surface loop (15 aa): pLDDT>=70, DSSP loop/turn, exposed junction residue (max RSA), indel-tolerant, 3D-clear of features

literature_notes: L2 and L3 both describe a C-terminal SYFP2 fusion to full-length TRPC5 that retains channel function (EC50 15 nM vs 20 nM for untagged). However, the topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residue 973) firmly in the intracellular span 625–973; a C-terminal tag therefore faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. This site is recorded in other_positions as intracellular. No ledger evidence supports any other extracellular junction (ECL0 is a single residue, ECL1 and ECL4 have no ledger-grounded insertion). Only L1 qualifies for a surface tag site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal SYFP2 fusion retains TRPC5 function (EC50 15 nM) but the C-terminus lies in the intracellular span 625–973 and is therefore not an extracellular surface tag site.
